mainEntity.name: Is this formula still considered accurate?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's a commonly used clinical reference, particularly for medication dosing, but it's a population average and doesn't account for individual differences in build or muscle mass.

mainEntity.name: Why do different ideal weight formulas give different results?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each formula (Devine, Robinson, Miller, Hamwi) was derived from different population data and uses slightly different constants, so results typically vary by a few kilograms between formulas for the same height. None is definitively 'correct' — treat them as general reference points rather than precise targets.

mainEntity.name: Is BMI or ideal weight formula more useful?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both have similar limitations — neither accounts for muscle mass or individual body composition, so pairing either with other measures like body fat percentage gives a fuller picture.

mainEntity.name: How does body frame size change ideal weight?

acceptedAnswer.text: A common convention subtracts 10% for a small frame and adds 10% for a large frame. You can estimate your frame from your wrist circumference and height with the body frame size calculator.
